title: Operational Failure Lens: transient vs persistent failure taxonomy, tracing hooks, and error surfaces
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: build an operationally-focused failure taxonomy and a set of error/latency surfaces that distinguish transient (retryable) vs persistent (actionable) failures across the inference stack. Deliverables: (1) tracing hook additions and semantic tags to enrich spans/metrics, (2) metrics + logs pipeline updates to emit classification fields, (3) a set of dashboards and alert rules (RecoveryClass, ErrorWaterfall, TailLatencyDrivers), and (4) runbook snippets mapping taxonomy -> remediation playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Tracing hooks instrumented so every inference span contains: model_version, model_variant, route, batch_id, queue_ms, kernel_fallback_flag, kv_cache_hit (y/n), and backend_status_code. 2) Metrics/log pipeline emits new fields failure_class and recovery_class and these fields are populated for >99% of error traces in synthetic test traffic. 3) Three dashboards (RecoveryClass surface, ErrorWaterfall per-route, TailLatency Drivers) exist in Grafana with supporting queries and documentation. 4) Pager/alert rules created for high-severity recovery_class=Persistent failures and automated runbook links attached. 5) Regression test validates mapping for timeouts, overload, decode/model errors, and HTTP/gRPC codes. 6) Rollout gated behind feature-flag and tested in staging then canaryed to 10% prod traffic without customer-visible regressions.
implementation_notes: Tracing: add span tags at two places: transport layer (http/grpc) for status codes and routing metadata; runtime executor for kernel_fallback_flag, kv_cache_hit, queue_ms. Use existing tracing lib wrapper to keep tag names stable. Metrics/log pipeline: update fluentbit config to map structured JSON logs and add a postprocessor lambda to compute recovery_class (Transient/Retryable, OverloadBackpressure, PersistentModelError, TransportFailure). Add a new Prometheus metric inference_failure_bucketed{recovery_class} for fast aggregation. Dashboards: Grafana panels will use prom queries + log-based panels for waterfalls. Alerting: SLO-aligned thresholds and a low-noise escalation path (first to oncall, then to platform-engineering).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + unit tests (2 weeks). 2) Deploy tracing hooks to staging; run synthetic failure scenarios (timeouts, overload with traffic shape, model decode errors) and verify tags (3 days). 3) Update pipeline and deploy to staging; verify metrics/alerts ingest (3 days). 4) Create dashboards and share with oncall for review (2 days). 5) Canary in prod 10% traffic for 48 hours; monitor for false positives/observability gaps. 6) Full rollout and documentation update. Rollback: disable feature flag + revert pipeline mapping if noise increases.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: increased cardinality from new span tags may raise ingestion cost and slow queries. Mitigation: cardinality budget and sampling rules applied; only include high-value tags at 100% and sample lower-value keys. Risk: incorrect recovery_class mapping leading to misrouted escalations. Mitigation: conservative default mapping (mark unknown as 'Investigate') and staged canary with synthetic validation. Risk: alert fatigue. Mitigation: tune thresholds during canary, add suppression windows and use composite alerts tied to SLO burn-rate.
notes: This ticket focuses on classification surfaces (how we present failures) rather than rewriting downstream incident playbooks. Work complements ENG-7246 (trace enrichment) but is distinct: taxonomy + dashboard UX + alerting. We will coordinate with PM Lina Gomez for runbook wording and with Support (Samir Reddy) for escalation flow.
